definitions.gloss: handing off entirely, complete delegation, dumping
definitions.explanation: Passing on a task or responsibility to someone else in its entirety, often without proper guidance or follow-up. Usually has a negative connotation.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}を{丸投|まるな}げする。
examples.english: To dump work entirely onto someone else.

examples.japanese: {外注|がいちゅう}{先|さき}に{丸投|まるな}げしてはいけない。
examples.english: You shouldn't just hand everything off to the outsourcing company.

examples.japanese: {責任|せきにん}を{部下|ぶか}に{丸投|まるな}げするのは{上司|じょうし}として{失格|しっかく}だ。
examples.english: A boss who dumps responsibility entirely on subordinates is unfit for the role.

notes:
{丸投|まるな}げ describes complete delegation without proper involvement.

ORIGIN: {丸|まる} (whole, entire) + {投|な}げる (to throw) - literally "throwing the whole thing."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {仕事|しごと}を{丸投|まるな}げする (dump work on someone)
- {丸投|まるな}げ{体質|たいしつ} (culture of passing the buck)
- {丸投|まるな}げ{委託|いたく} (complete outsourcing)

USAGE NOTE: Has a negative connotation, implying irresponsibility or laziness. More neutral terms like {委託|いたく} (commission) or {任|まか}せる (entrust) exist for appropriate delegation.
